raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Add native text-to-image inference for `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base`, including the latest DiT weights and small FLUX.2 decoder. Load its Diffusers component export through SGLang's standard component loaders and run the model through the native diffusion runtime.

## Modifications

- Register `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base` and `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-SFT` identifiers. End-to-end checkpoint evidence below covers Base only; SFT is name registration only until its weights are updated and validated.
- Expose `uncond_skip_layers` and `slg_*` through model-owned sampling fields and the existing Images API whitelist. DiT `skip_layers` is an internal forward argument.
- Register the pipeline, DiT, Qwen3.5 text encoder, training V2 nearest-grid Euler scheduler and sampling configuration. Keep flow shift 5, BF16 DiT/text encoder and FP32 VAE.
- Support ordinary CFG, two-pass skipped-unconditional guidance and three-pass additional skipped-conditional guidance. Defaults: CFG 3, layer 22 unconditional skipping, window 0.01–1.0. Ordinary CFG uses `uncond_skip_layers=[]`; three-pass uses CFG 5, `slg_layers=[22]`, `slg_scale=3`.
- Sampling defaults intentionally retain the recommended recipe used here: `slg_start=0.01` leaves the first denoising step at full CFG, and selecting three-pass SLG without an explicit `uncond_skip_layers` uses a complete unconditional branch so the extra skipped-conditional term is evaluated independently. The official pipeline at the tested revision defaults to `slg_start=0.0` and keeps unconditional skipping enabled even with three-pass SLG. Set `slg_start=0.0, uncond_skip_layers=[22]` explicitly to request that official behavior.
- Add exact DiT activation/normalization/RoPE fusion with numerical gates and eager fallback; precompute step-invariant conditioning and reuse the framework text-conditioning cache.
- Declare component residency and support DiT/text-encoder layerwise offload through existing managers. Reuse shared FLUX.2 VAE decoding helpers; LLaDA-Image only changes its helper import. The existing native VAE already accepts decoder channels 96/192/384/384 from the updated checkpoint.

## Accuracy Tests

**Numerical parity: with cuDNN SDPA disabled in both processes, the official reference and SGLang Torch SDPA produce identical float RGB (maximum absolute error 0) for all three guidance recipes.** An independent repeat also confirms that each reference policy is reproducible across two fresh processes. This validates the tested Base diet-guide workload; default FA comparisons are reported separately below.

On the final commit, 171 tests passed across `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_moss_image.py` and `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen3_5_encoder.py`. Pre-commit passes. Images API checks cover all three guidance recipes and a default request after three-pass; returned pixels match native offline output. The reproduction commands below were also run for all three recipes with both native default component backends and native Torch SDPA (six HTTP requests); all six outputs match the corresponding measured images. The new reference script reproduces all three controlled float-RGB outputs exactly. The displayed images, timing, offload and profile results were collected on an earlier revision with equivalent inference computation; the unit tests and API checks were rerun on the final commit. Component, DiT-only, text-encoder-only and combined layerwise offload preserve the resident float RGB output with `quality=exact`.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_moss_image.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen3_5_encoder.py
```

The reference is the unmodified `pipeline_moss_image.py` bundled at Base revision 355120bd6b44ff67b8df18f57e40b928fc886cd3, using Diffusers 0.38.0 for its small decoder. Native SGLang uses Diffusers 0.37.0 for configuration utilities and its own model/VAE implementation. PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and Transformers 5.19.0 are shared. All guidance arguments are explicit: the comparison uses slg_start=0.01, and three-pass reference calls set uncond_skip_layers=[] to keep the unconditional branch complete. These override the new reference's start=0 and unconditional-skip defaults.

Main images show the reference's original SDPA policy (cuDNN allowed), native Torch SDPA (framework cuDNN policy disabled), and native default FA. The main table therefore reports actual backend differences. A separate controlled lane disables cuDNN SDPA in the reference; all three guidance outputs are float-RGB identical to native SDPA, with matching branch order and layer 22 execution counts. SSIM uses float RGB in [0,1], a 7×7 local window, sample covariance and channel averaging; PSNR uses data_range=1. This single-prompt/seed agreement check is not a semantic-quality or GenEval benchmark. `quality=exact` does not imply equality across attention backends. Over 50 denoising steps, small floating-point differences between attention kernels can accumulate into composition changes; three-pass guidance can amplify them further. The matched-SDPA result isolates port correctness from those backend differences. The default request quality is `lossless`; these measurements explicitly use `exact`. MOSS-Image DiT fusions use bit-exact gates at either level, but the shared FLUX.2 VAE has additional quality-gated fast paths enabled at `lossless`, so the two end-to-end paths must not be treated as identical. No default-lossless pixel-parity result is claimed here.

### Reproduction

Use this PR's checkout with its diffusion dependencies installed. Native validation used PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0 and Diffusers 0.37.0. Run on one otherwise idle H200; the resident configuration needs approximately 33 GiB of GPU memory.

```bash
sglang serve --model-path OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base \
  --revision 355120bd6b44ff67b8df18f57e40b928fc886cd3 \
  --backend sglang --num-gpus 1 \
  --disable-autocast true --warmup-mode off --performance-mode manual \
  --component-residency all=resident \
  --served-model-name OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
```

Leave `--attention-backend` unset for the displayed default-attention results: on the tested H200 this selects `text_encoder: torch_sdpa` and `transformer: fa`. Setting it globally to `fa` also changes the text encoder and does not reproduce these images. Confirm these component choices in the startup log. For the matched-SDPA accuracy lane, restart with `--attention-backend torch_sdpa`; both components should then log `torch_sdpa`. Keep `quality=exact` and use the cuDNN-disabled reference below.

<summary>Reference pipeline: reproduce all three recipes</summary>

Use a separate environment with Diffusers **0.38.0**, PyTorch **2.14.1+cu130** and Transformers **5.19.0**, plus `huggingface_hub`, NumPy and Pillow. The tested reference uses Transformers' PyTorch fallbacks for causal convolution and gated delta attention (`causal_conv1d` and `flash-linear-attention` are not installed). Installing either package may change the reference's numerics; use the same dependency versions and keep both packages absent when reproducing the bit-exact result. Run from the directory containing the three request JSON files above. Save this as `moss_reference.py`; it loads the pinned checkpoint's own pipeline code and does not import SGLang.

```python
import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import numpy as np
import torch
from diffusers import AutoencoderKLFlux2
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--cudnn", choices=("enabled", "disabled"), default="disabled")
parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("reference-sdpa"))
args = parser.parse_args()
args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
# Run in a separate process that has not imported SGLang.
torch.backends.cuda.enable_cudnn_sdp(args.cudnn == "enabled")
model = Path(snapshot_download(
    "OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base",
    revision="355120bd6b44ff67b8df18f57e40b928fc886cd3",
))
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "reference_moss_image", model / "pipeline_moss_image.py"
)
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules[spec.name] = module
spec.loader.exec_module(module)
transformer = module.MOSSImageTransformer.from_pretrained(
    str(model / "transformer"), torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
).eval()
encoder = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    str(model / "text_encoder"), dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation="sdpa"
).eval()
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(str(model / "tokenizer"))
vae = AutoencoderKLFlux2.from_pretrained(
    str(model / "vae"), torch_dtype=torch.float32
).eval()
scheduler = module.MOSSImageScheduler.from_config(
    json.loads((model / "scheduler/scheduler_config.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
    shift=5.0,
)
pipe = module.MOSSImagePipeline(transformer, scheduler, encoder, tokenizer, vae).to("cuda")
for name in ("recommended", "ordinary", "three_pass"):
    req = json.loads(Path(f"{name}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    width, height = map(int, req["size"].split("x"))
    guidance = {key: req[key] for key in (
        "guidance_scale", "uncond_skip_layers", "slg_layers", "slg_scale",
        "slg_start", "slg_stop",
    ) if key in req}
    rgb = pipe(
        req["prompt"], width=width, height=height,
        negative_prompt=req["negative_prompt"],
        num_inference_steps=req["num_inference_steps"],
        generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(req["seed"]),
        output_type="np", **guidance,
    ).images
    np.save(args.output / f"{name}.npy", rgb)
    # Match the Images API's uint8 truncation when comparing downloaded PNGs.
    Image.fromarray(np.clip(rgb[0] * 255, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(
        args.output / f"{name}.png"
    )
    print(name, "saved", flush=True)
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The cached arm reuses the exact same positive/negative prompt; it is not cold-prompt latency. detail.body:
## Motivation

Add native text-to-image inference for `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base`, including the latest DiT weights and small FLUX.2 decoder. Load its Diffusers component export through SGLang's standard component loaders and run the model through the native diffusion runtime.

## Modifications

- Register `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base` and `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-SFT` identifiers. End-to-end checkpoint evidence below covers Base only; SFT is name registration only until its weights are updated and validated.
- Expose `uncond_skip_layers` and `slg_*` through model-owned sampling fields and the existing Images API whitelist. DiT `skip_layers` is an internal forward argument.
- Register the pipeline, DiT, Qwen3.5 text encoder, training V2 nearest-grid Euler scheduler and sampling configuration. Keep flow shift 5, BF16 DiT/text encoder and FP32 VAE.
- Support ordinary CFG, two-pass skipped-unconditional guidance and three-pass additional skipped-conditional guidance. Defaults: CFG 3, layer 22 unconditional skipping, window 0.01–1.0. Ordinary CFG uses `uncond_skip_layers=[]`; three-pass uses CFG 5, `slg_layers=[22]`, `slg_scale=3`.
- Sampling defaults intentionally retain the recommended recipe used here: `slg_start=0.01` leaves the first denoising step at full CFG, and selecting three-pass SLG without an explicit `uncond_skip_layers` uses a complete unconditional branch so the extra skipped-conditional term is evaluated independently. The official pipeline at the tested revision defaults to `slg_start=0.0` and keeps unconditional skipping enabled even with three-pass SLG. Set `slg_start=0.0, uncond_skip_layers=[22]` explicitly to request that official behavior.
- Add exact DiT activation/normalization/RoPE fusion with numerical gates and eager fallback; precompute step-invariant conditioning and reuse the framework text-conditioning cache.
- Declare component residency and support DiT/text-encoder layerwise offload through existing managers. Reuse shared FLUX.2 VAE decoding helpers; LLaDA-Image only changes its helper import. The existing native VAE already accepts decoder channels 96/192/384/384 from the updated checkpoint.

## Accuracy Tests

**Numerical parity: with cuDNN SDPA disabled in both processes, the official reference and SGLang Torch SDPA produce identical float RGB (maximum absolute error 0) for all three guidance recipes.** An independent repeat also confirms that each reference policy is reproducible across two fresh processes. This validates the tested Base diet-guide workload; default FA comparisons are reported separately below.

On the final commit, 171 tests passed across `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_moss_image.py` and `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen3_5_encoder.py`. Pre-commit passes. Images API checks cover all three guidance recipes and a default request after three-pass; returned pixels match native offline output. The reproduction commands below were also run for all three recipes with both native default component backends and native Torch SDPA (six HTTP requests); all six outputs match the corresponding measured images. The new reference script reproduces all three controlled float-RGB outputs exactly. The displayed images, timing, offload and profile results were collected on an earlier revision with equivalent inference computation; the unit tests and API checks were rerun on the final commit. Component, DiT-only, text-encoder-only and combined layerwise offload preserve the resident float RGB output with `quality=exact`.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_moss_image.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen3_5_encoder.py
```

The reference is the unmodified `pipeline_moss_image.py` bundled at Base revision 355120bd6b44ff67b8df18f57e40b928fc886cd3, using Diffusers 0.38.0 for its small decoder. Native SGLang uses Diffusers 0.37.0 for configuration utilities and its own model/VAE implementation. PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and Transformers 5.19.0 are shared. All guidance arguments are explicit: the comparison uses slg_start=0.01, and three-pass reference calls set uncond_skip_layers=[] to keep the unconditional branch complete. These override the new reference's start=0 and unconditional-skip defaults.

Main images show the reference's original SDPA policy (cuDNN allowed), native Torch SDPA (framework cuDNN policy disabled), and native default FA. The main table therefore reports actual backend differences. A separate controlled lane disables cuDNN SDPA in the reference; all three guidance outputs are float-RGB identical to native SDPA, with matching branch order and layer 22 execution counts. SSIM uses float RGB in [0,1], a 7×7 local window, sample covariance and channel averaging; PSNR uses data_range=1. This single-prompt/seed agreement check is not a semantic-quality or GenEval benchmark. `quality=exact` does not imply equality across attention backends. Over 50 denoising steps, small floating-point differences between attention kernels can accumulate into composition changes; three-pass guidance can amplify them further. The matched-SDPA result isolates port correctness from those backend differences. The default request quality is `lossless`; these measurements explicitly use `exact`. MOSS-Image DiT fusions use bit-exact gates at either level, but the shared FLUX.2 VAE has additional quality-gated fast paths enabled at `lossless`, so the two end-to-end paths must not be treated as identical. No default-lossless pixel-parity result is claimed here.

| Native backend | SSIM vs reference default policy | PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|
| Torch SDPA, cuDNN disabled | 0.80671 | 20.37 |
| Default FA | 0.81201 | 20.87 |

![Diet guide: reference, native SDPA, native FA](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5940cdd8-b1c7-45cc-8dbc-e61764669854)

| Guidance | Controlled SDPA float RGB | FA vs controlled reference SSIM | PSNR (dB) | DiT calls / layer 22 calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| recommended | Identical | 0.79524 | 19.78 | 100 / 51 |
| ordinary | Identical | 0.86967 | 21.98 | 100 / 100 |
| three_pass | Identical | 0.52907 | 14.43 | 149 / 100 |

Controlled comparisons: [recommended two-pass](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6efd0588-ac48-4b89-98e7-46af04d52bcc), [ordinary CFG](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9757c70-5b4e-4b10-87ad-bf88571c7405), [three-pass SLG](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc0edda7-a71f-4c02-b62e-722467eaace1).

### Reproduction

Use this PR's checkout with its diffusion dependencies installed. Native validation used PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0 and Diffusers 0.37.0. Run on one otherwise idle H200; the resident configuration needs approximately 33 GiB of GPU memory.

```bash
sglang serve --model-path OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base \
  --revision 355120bd6b44ff67b8df18f57e40b928fc886cd3 \
  --backend sglang --num-gpus 1 \
  --disable-autocast true --warmup-mode off --performance-mode manual \
  --component-residency all=resident \
  --served-model-name OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
```

Leave `--attention-backend` unset for the displayed default-attention results: on the tested H200 this selects `text_encoder: torch_sdpa` and `transformer: fa`. Setting it globally to `fa` also changes the text encoder and does not reproduce these images. Confirm these component choices in the startup log. For the matched-SDPA accuracy lane, restart with `--attention-backend torch_sdpa`; both components should then log `torch_sdpa`. Keep `quality=exact` and use the cuDNN-disabled reference below.

<summary>Reference pipeline: reproduce all three recipes</summary>

Use a separate environment with Diffusers **0.38.0**, PyTorch **2.14.1+cu130** and Transformers **5.19.0**, plus `huggingface_hub`, NumPy and Pillow. The tested reference uses Transformers' PyTorch fallbacks for causal convolution and gated delta attention (`causal_conv1d` and `flash-linear-attention` are not installed). Installing either package may change the reference's numerics; use the same dependency versions and keep both packages absent when reproducing the bit-exact result. import argparse

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import numpy as np
import torch
from diffusers import AutoencoderKLFlux2
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--cudnn", choices=("enabled", "disabled"), default="disabled")
parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("reference-sdpa"))
args = parser.parse_args()
args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
# Run in a separate process that has not imported SGLang.
torch.backends.cuda.enable_cudnn_sdp(args.cudnn == "enabled")
model = Path(snapshot_download(
    "OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base",
    revision="355120bd6b44ff67b8df18f57e40b928fc886cd3",
))
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "reference_moss_image", model / "pipeline_moss_image.py"
)
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules[spec.name] = module
spec.loader.exec_module(module)
transformer = module.MOSSImageTransformer.from_pretrained(
    str(model / "transformer"), torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
).eval()
encoder = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    str(model / "text_encoder"), dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation="sdpa"
).eval()
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(str(model / "tokenizer"))
vae = AutoencoderKLFlux2.from_pretrained(
    str(model / "vae"), torch_dtype=torch.float32
).eval()

    json.loads((model / "scheduler/scheduler_config.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
    shift=5.0,
)
pipe = module.MOSSImagePipeline(transformer, scheduler, encoder, tokenizer, vae).to("cuda")

        output_type="np", **guidance,
```

+Use a [SGLang Diffusion Docker environment](/docs/sglang-diffusion/installation).
+Until your image includes this integration, install the model-support PR inside

+## 2. Model capabilities
+
+MOSS-Image is a text-to-image model using Qwen3.5 text conditioning and a FLUX.2
+image decoder. Its native pipeline accepts natural-language prompts and structured
+layout descriptions through the same Images API. Structured prompts are passed
+to the text encoder as text, not interpreted as a separate rendering language.
+
+Choose Base for reproducing the reference comparison. The SFT identifier resolves
+to the same pipeline family, but its checkpoint has not been validated here.
+Generation is supported; image editing is not implemented. Keep the scheduler,
+guidance recipe, attention backend, and precision fixed when comparing outputs.
+
+## 3. Guidance and precision
+
+Defaults are 1024 x 1024, 50 steps, flow shift 5, CFG 3, and an empty negative
+prompt. Width and height must be divisible by 16. DiT and text-encoder weights
+use BF16; latents, CFG arithmetic, scheduler updates, and VAE decode use FP32.
+Autocast is disabled by the pipeline configuration; no extra CLI flag is needed.
+
+The default two-pass recipe skips unconditional layer 22 inside the
+`slg_start=0.01`, `slg_stop=1.0` window. It leaves the first step at full CFG.
+Set `uncond_skip_layers=[]` for ordinary CFG. Three-pass SLG adds a skipped
+conditional prediction and changes the sampling algorithm; it is not a lossless
+speed optimization.
+
+```json Three-pass request overrides
+{
+  "guidance_scale": 5,
+  "uncond_skip_layers": [],
+  "slg_layers": [22],
+  "slg_scale": 3,
+  "slg_start": 0.01,
+  "slg_stop": 1.0
+}
+```
+
+For the official pipeline's start-at-zero behavior, explicitly set
+`slg_start=0.0` and `uncond_skip_layers=[22]`, including when using three-pass
+SLG. Guidance fields are request-scoped and do not require a server restart.
+
+`quality=exact` preserves the native rounding policy, but does not make different
+attention backends identical. `quality=lossless` can additionally enable shared
+VAE fast paths. Compare each configuration against its matched reference rather
+than treating either quality name as a cross-backend guarantee.
+
+## 4. Deployment features
+
+Component and layerwise offload reuse the standard residency manager. Start with
+Auto placement; use `--component-residency all=resident` only when weights and
+request activations fit. Offload saves VRAM at the cost of host RAM and transfers.
+The text encoder also supports layerwise offload through its native layer list.
+
+Sequence parallelism uses the shared shard/pad/gather helpers and USP attention;
+the text refiner stays replicated. Ulysses degree must divide the 24 DiT heads.
+Ring requires a backend exposing softmax LSE, such as FlashAttention. CFG
+parallelism uses the shared branch dispatcher, including the optional third SLG
+branch. Multi-GPU checkpoint recipes remain experimental until measured on the
+selected hardware and workload.
+
+TP, Cache-DiT, quantization, LoRA, compilation, and breakable CUDA graphs do not
+have validated recipes in this integration. Do not assume that a framework-wide
+flag establishes model support. See [performance optimization](/docs/sglang-diffusion/performance-optimization)
+for the shared feature contracts.
+
+## 5. Batching
+
+Dynamic batching uses the shared scheduler and is opt-in through the maximum
+batch size. For example, on an H200:
+
+```bash
+sglang serve --model-path OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base \
+  --batching-max-size 4 --batching-delay-ms 20
+```
+
+Compatible requests may have different prompts and seeds; resolution, step count,
+negative prompt, and guidance settings must match. The maximum size limits total
+outputs, not just HTTP requests. A request can also use `n` to generate multiple
+images from one prompt. Higher batch sizes need more activation VRAM and can
+increase individual-request latency; the default remains one output at a time.
+
+At `quality=lossless` (the default) or `high`, the DiT groups samples by their actual text length
+and restores their original output order. Different lengths run in separate
+groups without padding or switching attention backends. Empty negative prompts
+can share one group even when positive prompts differ. The text refiner retains
+per-sample GEMM shapes to reduce numerical drift. Batched DiT GEMM shapes can
+change floating-point rounding, which denoising can amplify into visible changes;
+cross-batch-size pixel identity is not guaranteed. `quality=exact` retains the
+per-sample DiT path instead. Neither mode promises batch-invariant text encoding
+or VAE decoding. Benchmark your prompts and batch sizes before deployment.

+"""Fuse MOSSImage's bounded SiTU activation, preserving each BF16 rounding.
+
+The eager formula is ``4*tanh(gate/4)*sigmoid(gate) * 25*tanh(hidden/25)``.
+Each of its nine elementwise operations rounds to BF16. The operands may be
+separate projections or strided halves of one packed FFN projection.
+Large inputs use exact per-device tables for the two independent factors;
+small inputs and cold CUDA graph captures retain the direct fused formula.
+
+Verified on H200 for dense and packed rows with widths 128 and 8192,
+including [1, 6620, 8192], [1, 4109, 8192], [1, 2524, 8192] and
+[2, 65, 8192], plus every BF16 encoding of each operand.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import threading
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+from triton.language.extra.cuda import libdevice
+
+from sglang.kernels.numerics import (
+    mul_rn_f32,
+    round_bf16_to_fp32,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.common.platform import is_cuda
+from sglang.srt.utils.custom_op import register_custom_op
+
+_SITU_TABLES: dict[torch.device, tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = {}
+_SITU_TABLES_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+
+
+def _get_situ_tables(device):
+    tables = _SITU_TABLES.get(device)
+    if tables is not None:
+        return tables
+    if torch.compiler.is_compiling() or torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+        return None
+    with _SITU_TABLES_LOCK:
+        tables = _SITU_TABLES.get(device)
+        if tables is None:
+            # Enumerate bit patterns, not evenly spaced floating-point values.
+            # Generate with the live aten CUDA formula, including BF16 rounding.
+            values = (
+                torch.arange(65536, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+                .to(torch.int16)
+                .view(torch.bfloat16)
+            )
+            tables = (
+                25.0 * torch.tanh(values / 25.0),
+                (4.0 * torch.tanh(values / 4.0)) * torch.sigmoid(values),
+            )
+            # Publish only complete tables so subsequent streams need no wait.
+            # Keep their 256 KiB of storage for the process lifetime: captured
+            # graphs may retain these addresses after the originating request.
+            torch.cuda.current_stream(device).synchronize()
+            _SITU_TABLES[device] = tables
+    return tables
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _situ_lookup_kernel(
+    out_ptr,
+    hidden_ptr,
+    gate_ptr,
+    hidden_table,
+    gate_table,
+    numel,
+    hidden_row_stride,
+    gate_row_stride,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    offsets = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offsets < numel
+    rows, cols = offsets // DIM, offsets % DIM
+    hidden = tl.load(hidden_ptr + rows * hidden_row_stride + cols, mask, other=0).to(
+        tl.uint16, bitcast=True
+    )
+    gate = tl.load(gate_ptr + rows * gate_row_stride + cols, mask, other=0).to(
+        tl.uint16, bitcast=True
+    )
+    hidden_factor = tl.load(hidden_table + hidden.to(tl.int32)).to(tl.float32)
+    gate_factor = tl.load(gate_table + gate.to(tl.int32)).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, mul_rn_f32(gate_factor, hidden_factor), mask)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _tanh_bf16(value):
+    # tanh(x) rounds back to x in this range. Avoid libdevice's FTZ path so
+    # BF16 subnormals retain the same value as aten's tanh kernel.
+    return round_bf16_to_fp32(
+        tl.where(tl.abs(value) < 1.0e-4, value, libdevice.tanh(value))
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _situ_kernel(
+    out_ptr,
+    hidden_ptr,
+    gate_ptr,
+    numel,
+    hidden_row_stride,
+    gate_row_stride,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    offsets = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offsets < numel
+    rows, cols = offsets // DIM, offsets % DIM
+    hidden = tl.load(
+        hidden_ptr + rows * hidden_row_stride + cols, mask=mask, other=0.0
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    gate = tl.load(gate_ptr + rows * gate_row_stride + cols, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(
+        tl.float32
+    )
+
+    # Explicit non-FTZ multiplies also preserve subnormal intermediate values.
+    gate_quarter = round_bf16_to_fp32(mul_rn_f32(gate, 0.25))
+    gate_tanh = _tanh_bf16(gate_quarter)
+    gate_scaled = round_bf16_to_fp32(mul_rn_f32(gate_tanh, 4.0))
+    gate_sigmoid = round_bf16_to_fp32(tl.sigmoid(gate))
+    gate_factor = round_bf16_to_fp32(mul_rn_f32(gate_scaled, gate_sigmoid))
+    # This reciprocal and BF16 boundary match the eager scalar division.
+    hidden_scaled = round_bf16_to_fp32(mul_rn_f32(hidden, 1.0 / 25.0))
+    hidden_factor = round_bf16_to_fp32(mul_rn_f32(25.0, _tanh_bf16(hidden_scaled)))
+    result = mul_rn_f32(gate_factor, hidden_factor)
+    # The integer BF16 rounding helper is for finite values; preserve NaNs.
+    result = tl.where((hidden == hidden) & (gate == gate), result, float("nan"))
+    tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, result, mask=mask)
+
+

+    return is_cuda() and device.type == "cuda" and dtype == torch.bfloat16
+
+
+def _valid_situ_inputs(hidden: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    return (
+        is_cuda()
+        and hidden.is_cuda
+        and gate.is_cuda
+        and hidden.device == gate.device
+        and hidden.dtype == gate.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and hidden.shape == gate.shape
+        and hidden.ndim == 3
+        and hidden.numel() > 0
+        and hidden.stride(-1) == gate.stride(-1) == 1
+        and hidden.stride(0) == hidden.shape[1] * hidden.stride(1)
+        and gate.stride(0) == gate.shape[1] * gate.stride(1)
+        and hidden.stride(1) >= hidden.shape[2]
+        and gate.stride(1) >= gate.shape[2]

+
+def _fake_situ(hidden: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:

+    if not _valid_situ_inputs(hidden, gate):

+                gate.stride(1),

+                num_warps=4,
+                enable_fp_fusion=False,
+            )

+            out,
+            hidden,
+            gate,
+            hidden.numel(),
+            hidden.stride(1),
+            gate.stride(1),
+            DIM=hidden.shape[-1],
+            BLOCK=1024,
+            enable_fp_fusion=False,
+        )
+    return out

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""MOSSImage RMSNorm: FP32 statistics, BF16 rounding before learned scale.
+
+For widths 128/3072 with at least 16 rows, reproduce ATen's vectorized FP32
+mean reduction in one kernel. CUDA Reduce.cuh uses 32 lanes, four accumulators
+per lane, sequential fragment accumulation, then descending shuffle offsets.
+Other shapes retain ATen's mean with fused pointwise operations around it.
+Callers must verify against the live eager chain for each reduction regime.
+"""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+from sglang.kernels.numerics import cuda_rsqrtf, mul_rn_f32
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.common.platform import is_cuda
+from sglang.srt.utils.custom_op import register_custom_op
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _fold_halves(values, ROWS: tl.constexpr, WIDTH: tl.constexpr):
+    # Match shfl_down: first half + second half, largest offset first.
+    lo, hi = tl.split(tl.permute(tl.reshape(values, (ROWS, 2, WIDTH)), (0, 2, 1)))
+    return lo + hi
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _ordered_rstd(
+    X,
+    M: tl.constexpr,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    ROWS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    rows = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * ROWS + tl.arange(0, ROWS)
+    lanes = tl.arange(0, 32)
+    parts = tl.arange(0, 4)
+    acc = tl.full((ROWS, 32, 4), 0, tl.float32)
+    # ATen vectorizes the already-rounded FP32 squares, four per lane.
+    # Unroll to schedule loads ahead of the dependent accumulation chain.
+    for chunk in tl.static_range(DIM // 128):
+        cols = chunk * 128 + lanes[:, None] * 4 + parts[None, :]
+        x = tl.load(
+            X + rows[:, None, None] * DIM + cols[None, :, :], rows[:, None, None] < M, 0
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        acc = acc + mul_rn_f32(x, x)
+    even, odd = tl.split(tl.reshape(acc, (ROWS, 32, 2, 2)))
+    a, c = tl.split(even)
+    b, d = tl.split(odd)
+    total = ((a + b) + c) + d
+    total = _fold_halves(total, ROWS, 16)
+    total = _fold_halves(total, ROWS, 8)
+    total = _fold_halves(total, ROWS, 4)
+    total = _fold_halves(total, ROWS, 2)
+    total = _fold_halves(total, ROWS, 1)
+    mean = mul_rn_f32(tl.reshape(total, (ROWS,)), 1.0 / DIM)
+    return cuda_rsqrtf(mean + 1e-6)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _ordered_norm_kernel(
+    X,
+    Weight,
+    Out,
+    M: tl.constexpr,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    ROWS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    rows = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * ROWS + tl.arange(0, ROWS)
+    rstd = _ordered_rstd(X, M, DIM, ROWS)
+
+    cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = (rows[:, None] < M) & (cols[None, :] < DIM)
+    x = tl.load(X + rows[:, None] * DIM + cols[None, :], mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    weight = tl.load(Weight + cols, cols < DIM, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    normalized = mul_rn_f32(x, rstd[:, None]).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(
+        Out + rows[:, None] * DIM + cols[None, :],
+        mul_rn_f32(normalized, weight[None, :]),
+        mask,
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _norm_modulate_kernel(
+    X,
+    Weight,
+    Scale,
+    Shift,
+    Out,
+    M: tl.constexpr,
+    SEQ: tl.constexpr,
+    SCALE_STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    SHIFT_STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, 4096)
+    mask = cols < 3072
+    rstd = _ordered_rstd(X, M, 3072, 1)
+    x = tl.load(X + row * 3072 + cols, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    weight = tl.load(Weight + cols, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    norm = mul_rn_f32(x, tl.sum(rstd, 0)).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    norm = mul_rn_f32(norm, weight).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    scale = tl.load(Scale + (row // SEQ) * SCALE_STRIDE + cols, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    shift = tl.load(Shift + (row // SEQ) * SHIFT_STRIDE + cols, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    factor = (1.0 + scale).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    scaled = mul_rn_f32(norm, factor).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(Out + row * 3072 + cols, scaled + shift, mask)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _norm_rope_kernel(X, Weight, Cos, Sin, Out, M: tl.constexpr, HEADS: tl.constexpr):
+    rows = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * 16 + tl.arange(0, 16)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, 128)
+    mask = rows[:, None] < M
+    rstd = _ordered_rstd(X, M, 128, 16)
+    x = tl.load(X + rows[:, None] * 128 + cols[None, :], mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    weight = tl.load(Weight + cols).to(tl.float32)
+    norm = mul_rn_f32(x, rstd[:, None]).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    norm = mul_rn_f32(norm, weight[None, :]).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    lo, hi = tl.split(tl.permute(tl.reshape(norm, (16, 2, 64)), (0, 2, 1)))
+    half_cols = tl.arange(0, 64)[None, :]
+    rope_offsets = (rows // HEADS)[:, None] * 128 + half_cols
+    cos_lo = tl.load(Cos + rope_offsets, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    cos_hi = tl.load(Cos + rope_offsets + 64, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    sin_lo = tl.load(Sin + rope_offsets, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    sin_hi = tl.load(Sin + rope_offsets + 64, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    out_lo = mul_rn_f32(lo, cos_lo).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32) + mul_rn_f32(
+        -hi, sin_lo
+    ).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    out_hi = mul_rn_f32(hi, cos_hi).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32) + mul_rn_f32(
+        lo, sin_hi
+    ).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(Out + rows[:, None] * 128 + half_cols, out_lo, mask)
+    tl.store(Out + rows[:, None] * 128 + half_cols + 64, out_hi, mask)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _square_kernel(X, Squared, N: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    offsets = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    x = tl.load(X + offsets, offsets < N, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(Squared + offsets, mul_rn_f32(x, x), offsets < N)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _normalize_kernel(
+    X, Mean, Weight, Out, N: tl.constexpr, DIM: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr
+):
+    offsets = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offsets < N
+    x = tl.load(X + offsets, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    mean = tl.load(Mean + offsets // DIM, mask, 0)
+    weight = tl.load(Weight + offsets % DIM, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
+    normalized = mul_rn_f32(x, cuda_rsqrtf(mean + 1e-6))
+    # This rounding precedes gamma in MOSSImage, unlike conventional RMSNorm.
+    normalized = normalized.to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(Out + offsets, mul_rn_f32(normalized, weight), mask)
+
+

+def _chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+    query, key, value, g, beta, chunk_size=64, use_qk_l2norm=False
+):
+    """FP32 chunked prefill using the current Qwen3.5 triangular solve."""
+    initial_dtype = query.dtype
+    query, key, value, beta, g = [
+        x.transpose(1, 2).to(torch.float32, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)
+        for x in (query, key, value, beta, g)
+    ]
+    batch, heads, length, key_dim = key.shape
+    value_dim = value.shape[-1]
+    if use_qk_l2norm:
+        query = query * torch.rsqrt(query.square().sum(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)
+        key = key * torch.rsqrt(key.square().sum(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)
+    query = query * (key_dim**-0.5)
+    padding = (chunk_size - length % chunk_size) % chunk_size
+    query, key, value = [F.pad(x, (0, 0, 0, padding)) for x in (query, key, value)]
+    beta, g = [F.pad(x, (0, padding)) for x in (beta, g)]
+    num_chunks = (length + padding) // chunk_size
+    v_beta = value * beta.unsqueeze(-1)
+    k_beta = key * beta.unsqueeze(-1)
+    query, key, k_beta, v_beta = [
+        x.reshape(batch, heads, num_chunks, chunk_size, x.shape[-1])
+        for x in (query, key, k_beta, v_beta)
+    ]
+    g = g.reshape(batch, heads, num_chunks, chunk_size).cumsum(dim=3)
+    upper = torch.ones(
+        chunk_size, chunk_size, dtype=torch.bool, device=query.device
+    ).triu(1)
+    decay = (g.unsqueeze(4) - g.unsqueeze(3)).masked_fill(upper, float("-inf")).exp()
+    system = (k_beta @ key.transpose(-1, -2)) * decay
+    intra = (query @ key.transpose(-1, -2)) * decay
+    decayed_k_beta = k_beta * g.exp().unsqueeze(-1)

+        system, v_beta, upper=False, unitriangular=True
+    )
+    k_cumdecay = torch.linalg.solve_triangular(
+        system, decayed_k_beta, upper=False, unitriangular=True
+    )
+    state = torch.zeros(
+        batch, heads, key_dim, value_dim, dtype=values.dtype, device=values.device
+    )
+    output = torch.zeros_like(values)
+    query = query * g.exp().unsqueeze(-1)
+    key = key * (g[..., -1:] - g).exp().unsqueeze(-1)

+        v_new = values[:, :, i] - k_cumdecay[:, :, i] @ state

+    def forward(self, hidden_states, position_ids, rotary_emb, attention_mask):
+        batch, length, _ = hidden_states.shape
+        q, gate = (
+            self.q_proj(hidden_states)
+            .view(batch, length, self.num_heads, 2 * self.head_dim)
+            .chunk(2, dim=-1)
+        )
+        k = self.k_proj(hidden_states).view(
+            batch, length, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim
+        )
+        v = self.v_proj(hidden_states).view(
+            batch, length, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim
+        )
+        q, k = apply_qwen_vl_text_rope(
+            rotary_emb,
+            position_ids,
+            self.q_norm(q).transpose(1, 2),
+            self.k_norm(k).transpose(1, 2),
+        )
+        output = self.attn(
+            q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v, attn_mask=attention_mask
+        )
+        output = (
+            output.reshape(batch, length, -1)
+            * gate.reshape(batch, length, -1).sigmoid()
+        )
+        return self.o_proj(output)
+
+
+class Qwen3_5DecoderLayer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, config, layer_idx):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.layer_type = config.layer_types[layer_idx]
+        if self.layer_type == "linear_attention":
+            self.linear_attn = Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet(config)
+        elif self.layer_type == "full_attention":
+            self.self_attn = Qwen3_5Attention(config)
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported Qwen3.5 layer type: {self.layer_type}")
+        self.mlp = Qwen3VLTextMLP(config)
+        self.input_layernorm = Qwen3_5RMSNorm(
+            config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps
+        )
+        self.post_attention_layernorm = Qwen3_5RMSNorm(
+            config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps
+        )
+
+    def forward(
+        self, hidden_states, position_ids, rotary_emb, attention_mask, padding_mask
+    ):
+        residual = hidden_states
+        hidden_states = self.input_layernorm(hidden_states)
+        if self.layer_type == "linear_attention":
+            hidden_states = self.linear_attn(hidden_states, padding_mask)
+        else:
+            hidden_states = self.self_attn(
+                hidden_states, position_ids, rotary_emb, attention_mask
+            )
+        hidden_states = residual + hidden_states
+        return hidden_states + self.mlp(self.post_attention_layernorm(hidden_states))
+
+
+class Qwen3_5TextModel(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, config):
+        super().__init__()
+        if config.hidden_act != "silu":
+            raise ValueError("Qwen3.5 text encoding requires SiLU activation")
+        self.embed_tokens = nn.Embedding(
+            config.vocab_size, config.hidden_size, config.pad_token_id
+        )
+        self.layers = nn.ModuleList(
+            [Qwen3_5DecoderLayer(config, i) for i in range(config.num_hidden_layers)]
+        )
+        self.norm = Qwen3_5RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)
+        rope = dict(config.rope_parameters)
+        rope.setdefault("mrope_interleaved", True)
+        self.rotary_emb = get_rope(
+            head_size=config.head_dim,
+            rotary_dim=int(config.head_dim * rope.get("partial_rotary_factor", 1.0)),
+            max_position=config.max_position_embeddings,
+            base=rope["rope_theta"],
+            is_neox_style=True,
+            rope_scaling=rope,
+        )
+
+
+class Qwen3_5Model(TextEncoder):
+    """Qwen3.5 text-only prefill for diffusion conditioning."""
+
+    layer_names = ["language_model.layers"]
+    host_resident_table_names = ["language_model.embed_tokens"]
+
+    _supported_attention_backends = {
+        AttentionBackendEnum.FA,
+        AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA,
+    }
+
+    def __init__(self, config: Qwen3_5EncoderConfig):
+        super().__init__(config)
+        if config.quant_config is not None:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "Qwen3.5 diffusion encoder quantization is not supported"
+            )
+        self.language_model = Qwen3_5TextModel(config.arch_config.text_config)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def should_materialize_checkpoint_weight(name: str) -> bool:
+        return not name.startswith("visual.")
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
+        params = dict(self.named_parameters())
+        loaded = set()
+        for name, weight in weights:
+            if not self.should_materialize_checkpoint_weight(name):
+                continue
+            if name not in params:
+                raise KeyError(name)
+            loaded.add(load_stacked_weight(name, weight, params, ()))
+        return loaded
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids=None,
+        position_ids=None,
+        attention_mask=None,
+        inputs_embeds=None,
+        output_hidden_states=None,
+        use_cache=False,
+        return_dict=None,
+        past_key_values=None,
+        **kwargs,
+    ):
+        if output_hidden_states is None:
+            output_hidden_states = self.config.output_hidden_states
+        if return_dict is None:
+            return_dict = self.config.use_return_dict
+        if use_cache or past_key_values is not None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Qwen3.5 diffusion encoding does not use an autoregressive cache"
+            )
+        if (input_ids is None) == (inputs_embeds is None):
+            raise ValueError("Specify exactly one of input_ids or inputs_embeds")
+        if any(
+            kwargs.get(name) is not None
+            for name in (
+                "pixel_values",
+                "pixel_values_videos",
+                "image_grid_thw",
+                "video_grid_thw",
+            )
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Qwen3.5 diffusion encoder accepts text inputs only")
+        model = self.language_model
+        hidden_states = (
+            model.embed_tokens(input_ids) if inputs_embeds is None else inputs_embeds
+        )
+        batch, length, _ = hidden_states.shape
+        if position_ids is None:
+            position_ids = torch.arange(length, device=hidden_states.device)[
+                None
+            ].expand(batch, -1)
+        if position_ids.ndim == 2:
+            position_ids = position_ids[None].expand(3, -1, -1)
+        elif position_ids.shape[0] == 4:
+            position_ids = position_ids[1:]
+        padding_mask = attention_mask
+        if padding_mask is not None and bool(torch.all(padding_mask == 1)):
+            padding_mask = None
+        causal_mask = None
+        if padding_mask is not None:
+            causal_mask = torch.ones(
+                length, length, dtype=torch.bool, device=hidden_states.device
+            ).tril()
+            causal_mask = (
+                causal_mask[None, None] & padding_mask[:, None, None, :].bool()
+            )
+        all_hidden = () if output_hidden_states else None
+        for layer in model.layers:
+            if output_hidden_states:
+                all_hidden += (hidden_states,)
+            hidden_states = layer(
+                hidden_states, position_ids, model.rotary_emb, causal_mask, padding_mask
+            )
+        hidden_states = model.norm(hidden_states)
+        if output_hidden_states:
+            all_hidden += (hidden_states,)
+        if not return_dict:
+            return (
+                (hidden_states, all_hidden)
+                if output_hidden_states
+                else (hidden_states,)
+            )
+        return BaseEncoderOutput(
+            last_hidden_state=hidden_states, hidden_states=all_hidden
+        )
+
+
+EntryClass = Qwen3_5Model

+import math

+import torch
+from diffusers import FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler
+from diffusers.configuration_utils import register_to_config
+
+
+class MOSSImageScheduler(FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler):
+    """Euler integration using the training project's V2, nearest-grid schedule."""
+
+    @register_to_config
+    def __init__(self, num_train_timesteps=1000, shift=5.0, training_shift=1.0):
+        super().__init__(num_train_timesteps=num_train_timesteps, shift=1.0)
+        self.register_to_config(shift=shift, training_shift=training_shift)
+
+    def set_timesteps(self, num_inference_steps=50, device=None):
+        if (
+            not isinstance(num_inference_steps, int)
+            or num_inference_steps < 1
+            or not math.isfinite(self.config.shift)
+            or self.config.shift <= 0
+            or not math.isfinite(self.config.training_shift)
+            or self.config.training_shift <= 0
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Steps and shifts must be positive.")
+        total = self.config.num_train_timesteps
+
+        def grid(count, shift):
+            lower = shift / (total + shift - 1)
+            values = torch.linspace(1, lower, count)
+            return shift * values / (1 + (shift - 1) * values)
+
+        sigmas = grid(num_inference_steps, self.config.shift)
+        training = grid(total, self.config.training_shift).flip(0)
+        upper = torch.searchsorted(training, sigmas).clamp(max=total - 1)
+        lower = (upper - 1).clamp(min=0)
+        nearest = torch.where(
+            (sigmas - training[lower]).abs() <= (training[upper] - sigmas).abs(),
+            lower,
+            upper,
+        )
+        sigmas = torch.unique_consecutive(training[nearest])
+        # Our sigmas have already been shifted and snapped. Avoid a second shift.
+        self._shift = 1.0
+        super().set_timesteps(device=device, sigmas=sigmas.tolist())
+
+    def set_shift(self, shift):
+        if not math.isfinite(shift) or shift <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("shift must be positive")
+        self.register_to_config(shift=shift)
+
+    def scale_model_input(self, sample, timestep=None):
+        return sample
+
+
+EntryClass = MOSSImageScheduler

+class MOSSImageDenoisingStage(DenoisingStage):
+    @staticmethod
+    def _has_extra_slg(params: MOSSImageSamplingParams) -> bool:
+        return bool(params.slg_layers) and params.slg_scale > 0.0
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _has_dynamic_guidance(cls, params: MOSSImageSamplingParams) -> bool:
+        return cls._has_extra_slg(params) or (
+            bool(resolve_uncond_skip_layers(params))
+            and (params.slg_start != 0.0 or params.slg_stop != 1.0)
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _with_uncond_skip_layers(
+        cfg_policy: CFGPolicy, skip_layers: tuple[int, ...]
+    ) -> CFGPolicy:
+        if all(
+            branch.is_conditional
+            or tuple(branch.kwargs.get("skip_layers", ())) == skip_layers
+            for branch in cfg_policy.branches
+        ):
+            return cfg_policy
+        # Preserve the request-wide branches when changing one step's topology.
+        return replace(
+            cfg_policy,
+            branches=[
+                branch
+                if branch.is_conditional
+                else replace(
+                    branch, kwargs={**branch.kwargs, "skip_layers": skip_layers}
+                )
+                for branch in cfg_policy.branches
+            ],
+        )
+
+    def _predict_noise_with_cfg(
+        self,
+        current_model,
+        latent_model_input,
+        timestep,
+        batch,
+        timestep_index,
+        attn_metadata,
+        target_dtype,
+        current_guidance_scale,
+        cfg_policy,
+        cfg_gate_state,
+        server_args,
+        guidance,
+        latents,
+    ):
+        params = batch.sampling_params
+        active = (
+            params.slg_start <= timestep_index / len(batch.timesteps) < params.slg_stop
+        )
+        uncond_layers = resolve_uncond_skip_layers(params) if active else ()
+        cfg_policy = self._with_uncond_skip_layers(cfg_policy, uncond_layers)
+        # A cached CFG delta represents the old branch topology. Keep the
+        # reference's actual forwards when guidance changes within a request.
+        if self._has_dynamic_guidance(params):
+            cfg_gate_state = None
+        if not (active and self._has_extra_slg(params)):
+            return super()._predict_noise_with_cfg(
+                current_model=current_model,
+                latent_model_input=latent_model_input,
+                timestep=timestep,
+                batch=batch,
+                timestep_index=timestep_index,
+                attn_metadata=attn_metadata,
+                target_dtype=target_dtype,
+                current_guidance_scale=current_guidance_scale,
+                cfg_policy=cfg_policy,
+                cfg_gate_state=cfg_gate_state,
+                server_args=server_args,
+                guidance=guidance,
+                latents=latents,
+            )
+
+        config = server_args.pipeline_config
+
+        def predict(branch):
+            branch.configure_batch(batch)
+            with set_forward_context(
+                current_timestep=timestep_index,
+                attn_metadata=attn_metadata,
+                forward_batch=batch,
+            ):
+                prediction = self._predict_noise(
+                    current_model=current_model,
+                    latent_model_input=latent_model_input,
+                    timestep=timestep,
+                    target_dtype=target_dtype,
+                    guidance=guidance,
+                    **branch.kwargs,
+                )
+            return config.slice_noise_pred(prediction, latents).float()
+
+        slg_branch = replace(
+            cfg_policy.branches[0],
+            kwargs={
+                **cfg_policy.branches[0].kwargs,
+                "skip_layers": tuple(params.slg_layers),
+            },
+        )
+        expanded_policy = replace(
+            cfg_policy, branches=[*cfg_policy.branches, slg_branch]
+        )
+        predictions = (
+            run_cfg_parallel(expanded_policy, predict)
+            if server_args.enable_cfg_parallel
+            else [predict(branch) for branch in expanded_policy.branches]
+        )
+        noise_pred = cfg_policy.combine(
+            predictions[:-1],
+            batch,
+            config.get_classifier_free_guidance_scale(batch, current_guidance_scale),
+            config,
+            cfg_parallel=server_args.enable_cfg_parallel,
+        )
+        skipped = predictions[-1]
+        if not batch.do_classifier_free_guidance:
+            # Reference CFG=1 SLG uses the skipped prediction as its base.
+            noise_pred = skipped
+        return noise_pred + params.slg_scale * (predictions[0] - skipped)

+    def _before_denoising_loop(self, ctx, batch, server_args):

+        height, width = ctx.latents.shape[-2:]
+        with set_forward_context(0, None):

+    def component_uses(self, server_args, stage_name=None):

+            ComponentUse(
+                self._component_stage_name(stage_name),
+                "text_encoder",
+                memory_intensive=True,
+                start_at_stage_entry=False,
+            )
+        ]

+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def _encode_prompt(self, prompts, device, max_sequence_length=4096):
+        rows = []
+        for prompt in prompts:
+            formatted = self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+                [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
+                tokenize=False,
+                add_generation_prompt=True,
+                enable_thinking=True,
+            )

+                return_tensors="pt",

+                    component_name="text_encoder", module=self.text_encoder
+                )

+                    output = self.text_encoder(
+                        **inputs.to(device), use_cache=False, return_dict=True
+                    )
+                return output.last_hidden_state[0]
+
+            rows.append(
+                cached_encoder_call(
+                    self.text_encoder,
+                    (dict(inputs),),
+                    {"device": str(device)},
+                    encode_row,
+                    namespace=self,
+                    nested=False,
+                    share_in_group=True,

+            component_name="text_encoder", module=self.text_encoder
+        )
+        length = max(row.shape[0] for row in rows)
+        embeds = rows[0].new_zeros(len(rows), length, rows[0].shape[-1])
+        mask = torch.zeros(len(rows), length, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
+        for index, row in enumerate(rows):
+            embeds[index, : row.shape[0]] = row
+            mask[index, : row.shape[0]] = True
+        return embeds, mask
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _validate_request(batch, server_args):
+        params = batch.sampling_params
+        try:
+            valid_scale = math.isfinite(params.slg_scale) and params.slg_scale >= 0
+        except (TypeError, ValueError):
+            valid_scale = False
+        if not valid_scale:
+            raise ValueError("MOSSImage slg_scale must be finite and nonnegative.")
+        validate_skip_layers(

Added real DiT batching to the original branch (validated runtime `bfc534defcf8`), reusing the existing scheduler and attention/SP paths. Equal-length text contexts share a DiT forward; different lengths remain separate, with output order restored. Text refinement stays per sample to avoid its small-GEMM rounding drift. The default maximum batch size remains 1.

**Measured E2E throughput:** 1x H200, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, Base checkpoint revision `355120bd6b44ff67b8df18f57e40b928fc886cd3`, resident components, default attention, eager, `quality=lossless`. Four concurrent requests with distinct prompts/seeds, batch cap 4, 20 ms delay. One warmup wave, then 3 measured waves at 512 / 2 at 1024. Timing includes HTTP, PNG encoding, transfer and client decoding, not loading.

| Workload | Previous per-sample DiT | Grouped DiT |
|---|---:|---:|
| 512x512, 8 steps | 2.51 images/s | 2.92 images/s (+16%) |
| 1024x1024, 20 steps | 0.293 images/s | 0.296 images/s (essentially unchanged) |

This is not a cross-batch bit-exact optimization. After keeping text refinement per sample, **all four 1024-pixel outputs match the previous DiT path exactly**. At 512 pixels, agreement is **28.3-46.2 dB PSNR / 0.939-0.996 SSIM**. No semantic-quality conclusion follows from these agreement metrics, and other workloads can differ. The cookbook documents this explicitly. `quality=exact` retains per-sample DiT execution. Its 8 tested batch-4 PNGs match the previous implementation exactly; default batch-1 throughput stayed within 0.3% in the earlier control runs.

Final checks: **263 tests passed, 1 skipped** (requires two CUDA GPUs); **87 relevant CUDA kernel tests passed**, including the strided batch modulation fix. The final runtime also matches official controlled-SDPA float RGB exactly at 1024x1024 / 50 steps for all three guidance recipes plus a repeat. Repeated B4 HTTP requests with three-pass guidance also passed. These results do not establish batch invariance, multi-GPU checkpoint performance, or consumer-GPU performance; GPU model/performance baseline registration remains outstanding.
